detail:
A 2022 peer-reviewed review by Levine et al. in Occupational Therapy in Health Care describes occupational therapy as complementing physical therapy by addressing how a person functions day to day. The OT interventions the review lists include environmental modifications, adaptive equipment and orthoses, exercise and fall prevention, energy conservation and pacing, sleep hygiene, and routine/habit development.

Hand and wrist orthoses are described as "successful in limiting unwanted movement in hypermobile joints." Practical examples from the review include ergonomic wide-grip utensils, jar openers, shower chairs, and grab bars.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about whether occupational therapy is appropriate for you.
